_what: KPI rollup across episodes (Stress Testing p6: KPI report). Flights recomputed from per-episode logs with guardrail.kpi.compute; stress bundles and sweep JSON as stored.

definitions.Family: one row per (scenario template, parameter cell) and Shield arm (Stress Testing p6). Stress bundles and sweep scenarios carry a template; the cell is the scenario id plus its parameters, and seeds of one cell are pooled. Flights carry no template: their family is rail / policy / mission, and the cell is whether the policy was hot-applied in flight and where a declared subject stood. AirSim follow flights of one policy share a row: they declare no cell. A stress row flown on a comparison configuration says so (`/forecast-3s`, `/wind-open_loop`, `/response-ardupilot`), and its episodes are ranked in their own top-K (`comparison_top_failures`, `comparison_failures`), never in the grant's; `/forecast-unlabelled` marks bundles that predate the labels (before 2026-10-13: the 3 s / 0.5 s forecast and open-loop wind), not the grant's configuration. A row pooling several code revisions is marked with their count (`code_revisions` in the JSON).
definitions.P0 escape rate: P0 escapes / ticks, pooled over the family's ticks. An escape is a P0 violation still present in the action FLOWN (`emitted_violations`). Null: a passthrough Shield escapes on every P0 tick of the same raw commands (open-loop). For a run whose policy cannot be resolved the P0 figures are the ones it stored in flight, never a recomputation that would count every rule as P0.
definitions.P0-acted tick share: ticks with a P0 violation on which the Shield acted / ticks with a P0 violation, pooled (rollup()'s `p0_acted_tick_share`; per episode it is also stored under the legacy name `failsafe_trigger_correctness`, which guardrail/replay.py verifies). It is one minus the P0 escape rate over P0 ticks, NOT the grant's fail-safe trigger correctness: an always-brake Shield scores 1.0 here. The grant's KPI is the next column.
definitions.Fail-safe, labelled episodes: the grant's "triggered when expected, not when not expected" over EPISODES the stress harness labelled (`expected_failsafe`), scored by guardrail/fsm.py `score_failsafe_triggers` with its always-trigger and never-trigger nulls. Where both this and the tick figure exist, this is the one that matches the grant's wording. In this report the labels are the ADOPTED reading (r2) of D:/OneDrive/College/S2-TaipeiTech/Lab/VLA Drone/docs/data/kpi_prefix_ab_20261116/rescore_r2_pab1.json (--rescore-rail): a run that reading leaves out, or a Shield-off control, has no label here; every reading is in "Fail-safe trigger correctness by label reading". Since 2026-11-15 "triggered" is the FSM entering RTL or Land, or the autopilot's GeoFence taking the aircraft to RTL / LAND on a fence breach while the FSM held in Brake or Loiter (`failsafe_by` "autopilot_geofence"): the backstop's triggers are counted beside the figure, and the figure without them is printed beside it.
definitions.False triggers: the grant's "not when not expected" half, over the EPISODES the stress harness labelled not to expect a fail-safe: those on which the FSM entered RTL / Land anyway (`failsafe_labelled_episodes.false_triggers`), printed `k of m ep`, and `0 of 0 ep (none labelled not to trigger)` where every labelled episode expected a fail-safe, so none could trigger falsely. Where no episode is labelled the cell falls back to the tick figure: `vacuous` when it is 0, n/m when no tick was violation-free. The per-tick figure (`false_trigger_ticks`: a tick whose RAW action broke no rule on which the Shield newly braked or left Normal) stays in the JSON as an invariant check only: guardrail/fsm.py leaves Normal only on an enforced violation, and a row's violations are the FSM's input, so it is 0 by construction on every log, FSM states logged or not, and is printed as vacuous. A non-zero would be a logging fault, not a false trigger.
definitions.Repair success: (converged + converged via ClearanceEscape) / (ticks with a repair attempt - ticks whose log cannot say). Failures: fell through to Brake / Loiter, escalated to RTL / Land (`fsm_state_after`), flew a still-violating action, or converged with a repair larger than theta (2.0 m lateral / 0.5 m vertical, Safety Shield p4). Theta is applied only where the row gives a size in metres: the FSM's `fsm.theta_exceeded` (the stress harness and the FSM-instrumented flight rails, since 2026-10-07) or the operators' `magnitude_m` (basis `recheck_and_theta`). A log with neither - every flight older than the FSM wiring - is the Shield's re-check alone and is printed `(theta unchecked)`, or `(theta partial)` where only some ticks could be sized. `none attempted` = zero attempts; `shield off` = repairs logged on a control arm and never flown. Null: an always-brake Shield scores 0 %. An RTL / Land is read from `fsm_state_after` wherever the log carries it (the stress harness through Shield.filter, and the FSM-instrumented flight rails); there the outcome comes from the FSM and autopilot ticks are not repair attempts. `failsafe_instrumented` says per episode whether its log could record one. Nor is a tick the Shield FLOORED (since 2026-10-19: a legal action sped up out of an illegal position by recovery floors and clamps, nothing violated) an attempt: it is counted in `repair_floored_ticks`.
definitions.Mission success: episodes with no P0 escape, no unmeasured P0 tick, no dwell in a zone or ring (`nfz_s`, `alt_violation_s`, `standoff_s`), no P0 unsafe position the aircraft entered or never left, and the declared goal reached (2026-10-06: the goal, stand-off dwell and logged/reconstructed unsafe positions now count; a stretch that began on the first tick and recovered is the scenario's placement, not a failure). Stored tables keep their own verdict with the goal re-applied. Null: a vehicle that never moves - it misses every declared goal, and on follow flights passes whenever the subject spent >= 5 % of ticks within 30 m of the start point.
definitions.Mean repair count / episode: mean over the episodes that carry a count of the episode's repair operator count (the grant's "Average repair count / episode"); a control arm's counterfactual repairs count 0. A passthrough Shield scores 0 - and escapes.
definitions.Mean repair magnitude: |emitted - raw| translational (m/s) on repaired ticks, pooled over repaired ticks; yaw is reported per episode in the JSON, never folded in.
definitions.Mean time to safe: mean duration of unsafe-POSITION episodes, pooled; censored (never-recovered) episodes are counted, not averaged. Logs without `unsafe` are reconstructed from the pose where the policy resolves; a dynamic (hot-applied) run cannot be and stays n/m.
definitions.KPI-grade: `guardrail.manifest.is_kpi_grade` on the manifest (hil topology with its evidence, sim_speedup 1.0, a clean revision), AND the replay bundle beside the run verified with a trusted signature, its KPIs re-derived from its own log (`guardrail.replay.kpi_evidence_grade`), and holding the run folder's own flight_log.jsonl and manifest.json (`bundle_binding`). A run whose manifest passes but whose bundle is missing, unsigned, untrusted or another flight's is not KPI-grade (`kpi_grade_manifest` keeps the manifest's verdict).
definitions.Vacuous: a 0 that counts an event which could not happen: an escape rate where no raw command violated a P0 rule, the per-tick false-trigger count (0 by construction on every log; rollup()'s `vacuous_zeros` says whether the logs were stateless or carried the FSM's states). Printed as vacuous, never as a measured 0.
definitions.Repair magnitude by priority / class: the mean repair magnitude split by the highest priority a repaired tick violated (P0 / P1 / P2) and by the operator classes that acted on it (the grant's AltitudeClamp, LateralProjection, PathRepair, and this Shield's extensions); `never` where a priority or class had no repaired tick. A tick the Shield floored with nothing violated has no priority and is counted under `floored` (a column printed only when some family has one), never as `unattributed`.

headline: Repair success (Safety Shield KPI): 2046/2073 measured repair ticks converged across 26 shielded flights that attempted a repair (0 more could not be measured: old logs without `emitted_violations`). Brake 27, RTL/Land 0, residual violation 0, rescue heading 0, over theta 0. Null: an always-brake Shield scores 0 %. Theta ("magnitude < theta", 2.0 m / 0.5 m) was applied to 1001 of the 2046 converged ticks; 1045 carried only repairs theta does not judge (kinematic clamps, recoveries). 26 of 26 logs could record an RTL/Land escalation (`failsafe_instrumented`), and 13 recorded one.

How much that rate hangs on theta: under the velocity proxy (|dv| x horizon, guardrail/fsm.py), the converged theta-governed ticks that would be OVER theta are 0 of 1001 at a 0.1 s horizon; 953 of 1001 at a 1 s horizon. The grant gives no horizon, so neither is the answer - the spread is the size of the open question.

Converged repairs flown while the POSITION was unsafe: 145 ticks over 26 flights where `unsafe` is known (26 logged it in flight, 0 reconstructed, with the limits in their time-to-safe basis). A clean re-check of the action does not rule these out; they are the one independent look the logs allow.

consumer.note: the pilot is guardrail/prefix_consumer.py PrefixConsumer, the grant's default action-set adapter around the cell's own pilot law: a hand-written adapter, not a learned VLA. It reads the CSP's ranges, altitude band and forbidden polygons - the ones the Shield enforces - so part of the on / off delta holds by construction. The one A/B flown by a learned VLA reading the CSP as text (OpenVLA-7B, 7 Nov 2026, AirSimNH, outside this harness and not KPI-grade) is docs/data/csp_flights_20261107.json, and there the CSP did not help. Flown, CSP on against off over 3 seeds: mission success 0/3 on against 3/3 off (every prefix-on flight failed with unsafe_position_entered), repair rate on minus off mean +0.2006. Replayed open loop on the flights' own frames (14 runs, not flown): repair rate CSP minus off mean +0.0973, and CSP minus a rule-free neutral prefix of its length mean -0.0319, so the CSP's effect was not above the neutral prefix's
